data.body:
MERGED — Gerrit 1316 (`2ca9: price provider-qualified usage rows`), on main.

THE FIX: `_pricing_model_ref` delegates to `config.split_provider_qualifier`, which decides purely by
membership in KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES. No second parser, no prefix matching, and the LookupError -> unpriced
policy is untouched. `summarize` now NAMES each unresolvable ref in its footer, so a genuinely-unknown model
reads bare (`my-local-model`) while a mis-formatted id keeps its malformation visible
(`not-a-provider:m`) — that is AC5's "distinguishable" requirement made observable rather than asserted.
An AST guard mirroring the attested capabilities one bans `.split(":")` / `.partition(":")` and the provider
literals across usage_log.py.

RED, before the fix, against real genai-prices:
    PASSED  [bedrock-bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-...]
    FAILED  [anthropic-anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6-...]  priced as unpriced
    FAILED  [openai-openai:gpt-5.4-...]                  priced as unpriced
    FAILED  test_bedrock_stays_dearer_than_anthropic_for_the_same_model  assert (None is not None)
    5 failed, 3 passed
The bedrock-passes / anthropic-and-openai-fail split reproduces the reported asymmetry exactly. After:
61/61 usage-log tests pass and a real 4-row log renders $0.0105 / $0.0115 / $0.0100 with
"est. cost excludes 1 unpriced call. No pricing data for: my-local-model."

CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN STATED RATIONALE — recorded because I wrote the wrong reason and it was
caught. The plan claimed a blind `split(":")` "would break the one provider that currently works" because
the Bedrock remainder `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` is not genai-prices' AWS id shape. THAT IS FALSE: I
measured it at $0.00495, byte-identical to the prefixed form — genai-prices' fuzzy match resolves it fine.
The constraint survives on a DIFFERENT and stronger case found during implementation: the versioned AWS id
`anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` prices today at $0.00165, and a blind first-colon split reduces
it to `"0"`, which LookupErrors. The AC4 test pins that real case rather than the plan's invented one.
